examples.scenario: Malicious code inserted into a widely used open-source software library by a compromised third-party developer, resulting in a backdoor implant that exfiltrates environment variables and sensitive tokens to attacker-controlled C2 upon initialization.

version_control_commit_log.author: john.smith <john.smith@trustedvendor.com>
version_control_commit_log.message: Update config loader with new feature

examples.detection_method: Monitor software supply chain repositories for unexpected commits modifying core library functions; verify code integrity using SBOM hashes; detect anomalous outbound HTTPS POST requests from developer build environments or runtime processes to unknown external domains; implement network egress filtering and SSL/TLS interception to inspect suspicious encrypted traffic; utilize endpoint detection to flag process spawning node.js HTTP requests to unrecognized hosts.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1195.002 - Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
